name: ch30_anniversary_host_role
alt: A young man proudly holds a clipboard and runs a 50th anniversary evening while an elderly uncle gives the speech at the mic.
scene: A wide view of a decorated community hall at an Indian 50th wedding anniversary party in the evening. Centre-back, a small stage with a marigold garland arch and a banner showing a big gold "50"; an elderly grandparent couple sit on two decorated chairs, the grandmother in a cream silk sari, the grandfather in a white kurta, both smiling. To the left of the stage the eldest uncle, in his sixties with grey hair and a brown Nehru jacket, stands at a microphone stand reading from a folded paper. In the foreground right, the cousin, a man in his late twenties in a maroon kurta, stands tall and proud holding a clipboard with a running order and a cordless microphone, one arm pointing to direct a caterer carrying a tray of sweets and a cousin carrying the cake towards the stage. A dashed arrow runs from him to the cake, another to the caterer, showing that he is moving the whole programme. Behind him, his mother in a green sari gives a small approving nod. A small inset bubble near the cousin shows a clipboard with three ticked lines. Warm string lights overhead, festive and happy mood. Labels: "HOST" above the cousin, "SPEECH" above the uncle at the mic.

key: A housing society in Pune wants to repaint
name: ch30_society_colour_committee
alt: Split picture: a repaint plan announced by three people is rejected by angry residents; next year the same plan, led by the former critic, is approved.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line, the same four-storey housing society building in Pune in both halves, beige walls with balconies and potted plants. LEFT panel: in the foreground three people, the secretary in a white shirt and two friends, stand close together holding a single paint swatch card and a phone showing a group chat announcement; facing them a small crowd of four residents, an older man in a vest, a woman in a salwar kameez, a young man and an aunty with folded arms, frown and raise their hands in protest; a big red cross floats over a ballot box at the side. RIGHT panel: one year later, the same building is half painted a fresh teal, a painter on a ladder; the former loudest critic, the older man now in a neat shirt, holds the same swatch card and points proudly at the wall while the other residents smile and raise their hands to vote yes; a green tick floats over the ballot box. Morning light, calm and cheerful on the right, tense on the left. Labels: "ANNOUNCED" at the top of the left panel, "INVITED" at the top of the right panel.

key: fold the laundry, so she offers him
name: ch30_laundry_pay_backfire
alt: A boy earns coins for folded laundry and is caught pulling clean shirts off hangers to fold them again for more money.
scene: A bright bedroom in a Chennai flat in the afternoon. On the left, a plastic laundry basket stacked with perfectly folded shirts and a small steel bowl holding a few coins, with a handwritten note card on the wall reading "+10 / -2". In the centre, a boy of about ten in a yellow T-shirt and shorts stands at an open wooden cupboard, sneakily pulling an already clean, ironed shirt off a hanger, a pile of re-folded shirts at his feet. A dashed arrow loops from the hanger to the folding pile and to the coin bowl, showing the shirts going round and round for money. In the doorway on the right, his mother, in her late thirties in a blue cotton sari with her hair in a plait, stands with one hand on her hip and the other on her forehead, eyebrows raised, half amused and half dismayed. A small exclamation badge hovers above her. A ceiling fan and a window with green curtains in the background; on the floor near the cupboard, a few crumpled shirts that were never the problem lie forgotten. The mood is gently comic: the rule worked too well. Labels: "PAID PER BASKET" above the basket on the left.

key: takeaway order of 40 for an office party
name: ch30_dosa_stall_referral
alt: A busy dosa stall owner apologetically declines a bulk order and hands the customer a card with his brother-in-law's number; the customer leaves smiling.
scene: A street-side dosa stall in old Bengaluru in the morning, a steel counter, a huge flat iron griddle with three crisp dosas, a steaming steel container of chutney and a small queue of customers. Behind the counter, the owner, a man in his fifties with a moustache, white vest and a checked lungi, leans forward warmly, one hand on his heart in a gentle apology and the other handing a small white visiting card across the counter. In front of the counter, the customer, an office worker in her early thirties in a lavender kurta with a lanyard and a phone, takes the card with a pleased smile. A small thought bubble near her shows a stack of dosas and a little calendar page reading "SUN". On the right edge, a dashed arrow runs from the card along a little street map with two turns to a second small stall with the same griddle and an awning. Warm morning sunlight and steam rising; nobody is upset, the refusal feels like help. Labels: "NOT TODAY" over the first stall, "TRY HIM" over the second stall at the end of the arrow.

key: the boy who keeps throwing chalk in class
name: ch30_chalk_monitor
alt: Before and after: a boy throws chalk in a Kerala classroom, then as class monitor guards the chalk box and scolds a classmate for wasting chalk.
scene: A split-panel illustration of the same Kerala school classroom, green blackboard, wooden benches, windows with coconut palms outside, divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: a mischievous boy of about eleven in a white shirt and navy shorts uniform stands on a bench mid-throw, a piece of chalk flying in a dashed arc toward another student, who ducks; the teacher, a woman in a cream-and-gold sari, looks back from the board with a frown. RIGHT panel: one week later the same boy stands in front of the blackboard wearing a small badge on his shirt, holding the wooden chalk box under one arm and wagging a finger at a classmate who has dropped a broken piece of chalk on the floor; behind him the board is wiped clean and neat. The teacher in the corner smiles. A small arrow curves from the flying chalk on the left to the chalk box on the right, showing the same energy redirected. Bright daylight, playful mood. Labels: "BEFORE" at the top of the left panel, "MONITOR" at the top of the right panel, on the boy's badge only a small star.

key: A good wedding caterer in Hyderabad
name: ch30_caterer_listens_first
alt: A wedding caterer listens and takes notes with a family before pointing to a live dosa counter, with steps from needs to benefit shown above.
scene: A family living room in Hyderabad in the evening. On the right, the bride's family sits on a sofa: a father in his fifties in a white kurta, a mother in a red silk sari, and a young woman, the bride, in a pink salwar. On the left, the caterer, a man in his forties in a neat blue shirt with a small notebook and pen, sits forward on a chair listening carefully, the notebook showing "500" and a leaf symbol for vegetarian. On a low glass table between them lies an open brochure with three package cards. Above the scene runs a row of four small round icons joined by arrows, left to right: an ear (listening to needs), a heart (what they care about), a list (packages), and a sparkling plate (the benefit). In a thought bubble above the caterer, a live dosa counter with a cook and a line of happy guests. On the far left, a small kitchen inset shows a big pot labelled "300" honestly, not 500. The father leans in, interested, as the caterer finally speaks. Warm lamp light, friendly mood. Labels: "LISTEN FIRST" above the four icons.

key: clean his room before relatives visit
name: ch30_nephew_trophies_room
alt: Split picture: a teenager rolls his eyes at an order to clean; then, told the cousins will see his cricket trophies, he sighs and tidies his room.
scene: A split-panel illustration of a teenager's bedroom, divided by a thin vertical line, the same messy room in both halves: clothes piled on the bed and a chair, a cricket bat leaning on the wall, and a shelf of small gold cricket trophies half hidden behind a heap of T-shirts. LEFT panel: the aunt or uncle, a woman in her forties in a mustard salwar kameez, stands at the doorway pointing at the mess with a stern face; the nephew, about fifteen in a grey hoodie and shorts, lies on the bed scrolling his phone and rolls his eyes, a small speech bubble with only a red cross. RIGHT panel: the same adult now sits on the edge of the desk, calm, gesturing at the trophy shelf; a small inset bubble shows two younger cousins admiring trophies and a calendar page with "SUN" and a cricket ball. The nephew, sighing with puffed cheeks, carries an armful of clothes to the cupboard and the trophies are now visible and shining. Not delighted, just willing. Daylight through a window. Labels: "ORDER" at the top of the left panel, "HIS REASON" at the top of the right panel.

key: keeps getting out to the short ball
name: ch30_coach_nine_steps
alt: A cricket coach quietly encourages a young batsman in the nets, with a path of nine numbered stepping stones leading to a district team cap.
scene: A practice net at a local cricket ground in the late afternoon, green turf, a long net tunnel and a few senior players far away in the background practising, unaware. In the foreground left, a young batsman of about sixteen in white clothes, pads and a helmet held under his arm, listens with a hopeful face. Beside him, the coach, a man in his fifties with grey stubble, a cap and a track suit, rests a hand on the boy's shoulder and makes a small gesture with his other hand showing a tiny movement, as if shifting the back foot an inch. Behind them, a ball pitches short and rises toward an empty batting crease, with a dashed arrow showing a batsman's sway out of its path. Across the lower foreground runs a curving path of nine small round stepping stones numbered 1 to 9, leading right to a pedestal with a dark blue cricket cap on it. A small inset bubble near the coach shows a thumbs-up. Golden low sunlight and long shadows, a warm, private, encouraging mood. Labels: "DISTRICT TEAM" above the cap on the pedestal at the end of the stones.
